title: TissueCyte Installation And Alignment Guide
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science

materials: Always wear PPE when using the system.

Warning: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) should be used at all times while operating this protocol. If you are unsure what PPE you should be using, see your immediate supervisor or the Institute laser safety officer.
Unplug X-CMD and Y-CMD cables from scanner box
Two beams indicate need for dichroic alignment
Plug X-CMD, Y-CMD cables back in
Reset laser to appropriate wavelength and power
Change the V2 voltage (either at Vivace software (ref. Fig. above) or at the LCR controller (Ref. Figure below)) to maximize power again. Note the V2 value that gives you maximum.
Phase Adjustment to Align Left/Right Scans
This procedure is to be performed through Orchestrator
Shut down Windows and power off the PC.
Replace the PC in the rack.

steps.title: Initial Laser Activation
steps.instruction: Activate the laser and open the shutter to prepare for alignment.

substeps.instruction: Open Spectra Physics Mai Tai software and click and hold the 'ON' button for 3 seconds.
Wait approximately 30 minutes for the laser power to stabilize.
Click and hold the Shutter button for 3 seconds to open the shutter.
Turn the laser power to a lower level.

steps.title: General Laser Path Alignment
steps.instruction: Align the laser path sections sequentially, starting from the source and moving toward the end.

substeps.instruction: Set the wavelength to 700 um (visible red) in the wavelength window.
Adjust pinholes P1 and P2 to be very small (do not move their location unless necessary).
Adjust the angle of mirror M1 until the light path is aligned for P1 via visual inspection.
Open pinhole P1 and adjust the angle of mirror M2 until the light path is aligned for P2 via visual inspection.
Iterate M1 and M2 adjustments until perfect alignment is achieved.
Change wavelength to 925-950 um (invisible IR) and repeat the alignment procedure using an IR viewer and IR sensor card.
Ensure all pinhole apertures are fully open before proceeding to the next section.

steps.title: Scanning Mirror Reset
steps.instruction: Reset the scanning mirror positions before beginning the next alignment phase.

substeps.instruction: Turn OFF the scanner box and wait 30 seconds.
Turn ON the scanner box (the mirror position resets automatically when turned on without an input signal).

steps.title: X-Scanner and Objective Alignment
steps.instruction: Align the beam through the scanning system and objective.

substeps.instruction: Ensure laser is on and open the shutter.
Use half wave plates to set laser power to a lower level (<50mW).
Set wavelength to ~700 um (visible red).
Remove down mirror (M4) located just upstream of the X-scanner.
Close irises on pinholes and examine alignment on the far pinhole (beyond down mirror).
Use the far mirror (top of periscope) to increase the misalignment vector (magnitude and direction) on the far pinhole.
Adjust near mirror (M3) to bring the beam back into the center of the near pinhole.
Verify that P3, P4, and M3 fall along a straight line, and M3 and M4 fall along a perpendicular straight line.
Place a partially transparent sheet with a bulls-eye behind the objective to examine beam centering.
Place a sheet of paper behind the objective to examine for beam aberrations.
Place an opaque card with a punched hole where the laser enters the TC system; a single reflected beam indicates the system is well aligned.
If the dichroic is misaligned, adjust the screws on the front and side of the plate upstream of the objective to align the reflected beam with the incident beam.
Turn the scanner box OFF, wait 30 seconds, reinstall the down mirror, and fully open the pinholes.

steps.title: Beam Expander Adjustment
steps.instruction: Adjust the Beam Expander (BE) located as the last element on the laser path before the deflecting mirror (M).

substeps.instruction: Fine-adjust the mounting angle using the three screws (S) on the mounting hardware (ensure it is mounted in reverse, following the laser direction).
Slowly turn the adjusting ring to adjust the beam width.

steps.title: Liquid Crystal Retarder (LCR) Installation
steps.instruction: Install and calibrate the LCR to allow specific laser power to reach the sample.

substeps.instruction: Mount LCR on the table perpendicularly to the optical axis so the beam hits approximately the center of the crystal.
Place a power meter sensor at the objective output.
Rotate the LCR mount to maximize power and note the maximum value.
Power up the LCR by clicking 'OPEN' at the LC Shutter State tab of the Vivace window.
Set V2 to allow 250 +/- 10mW at the objective output (ideally allowing ~270mW total).

steps.title: Cable Replacement
steps.instruction: Replace system cables with care to avoid mechanical stress.

substeps.instruction: Power down the specific component and shut down both Master and Slave computers and all electronics.
Remove side panels of the TissueCyte box if necessary (e.g., left side for piezo controller cable).
Install the new cable, ensuring no mechanical stress and taking up any slack to prevent drooping into the optical path.
Power up the system and thoroughly test the replaced component.
Discard or mark the old cable as defective.

steps.title: PC Component Card Replacement
steps.instruction: Replace internal PC component cards using anti-static precautions.

substeps.instruction: Remove all cables from the back of the computer, using tape labels to identify connectors.
Remove the PC from the rack and place it on a grounded anti-static mat.
Wear a wrist strap to stay grounded.
Open the PC and disconnect internal cables from the card to be replaced.
Unscrew the capture screw and remove the card; place it in an anti-static bag.
Insert the new card into the slot and secure it with the capture screw.
Reconnect internal cables, close the PC enclosure, and reconnect external cables.
Power on the PC and run tests to verify connectivity and card functionality.

steps.title: Microsphere Slide Setup and Alignment
steps.instruction: Use a microsphere slide to calibrate the stage tilt and image area.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve the microsphere slide from the TissueCyte refrigerator.
Place the 5x5 inch tip-tilt stage on a level surface and use two spirit levels and the two micrometer screws to make it horizontal.
Tape the slide onto the tip-tilt stage to prevent movement.
Apply distilled water to the center of the slide to form a meniscus.
Place the stage on the XY platform, bring the sample area below the objective, and raise the stage until the lens touches the water meniscus.
Turn off lights, turn on PMT voltage, and acquire a 2D image via the Orchestrator window.
Adjust Z-stage height until microspheres (approx. 8 pixels in diameter) are focused.
Move a small group of spheres across the image area (Left-Right-Backward-Forward) using Orchestrator Stage Control.
If intensity changes across the field, finely adjust the corresponding micrometer knob (1 graduation or less) until intensity is constant; repeat for the perpendicular axis.
Measure the total distance (microns) between edges by moving a sphere from one edge to another in both axes (expected area: 750 to 780 microns square).
Determine x-overlap and y-overlap by capturing a 3D Mosaic in the Imaging tab with settings from the Protocol tab and inspecting adjacent tiles.

steps.title: PMT Trim Adjustment
steps.instruction: Adjust the PMT noise threshold to maximize signal-to-noise ratio.

substeps.instruction: Locate the trim setting dial inside the PMT assembly casing.
Set the Trim dial to 9 (optimal for the 18 operational detectors).
Only re-adjust if noise levels are excessively high after checking for external noise sources or software artifacts.
